title: Ship Encyclopedia

bb.title: Battleship
bb.body: The armoured gun platform: the largest guns and the hardest single hits, paid for with long reloads and sluggish handling. Angle your belt so incoming AP bounces, and aim at an enemy's midships citadel to get full damage; HE starts fires and grinds down angled targets. Most battleships carry no torpedoes and no smoke, so she suffers once spotted and focused, and destroyer torpedoes are lethal.

cv.title: Aircraft Carrier
cv.body: A carrier fights entirely through her aircraft: air groups are finite — flak that wipes a squadron takes all your damage with it — so strike and leave. The hull has almost no guns of her own: she survives on distance and cover, and her real value is spotting and cross-map pressure.

1.text: Each number picks a different aircraft type; double-tap to launch the squadron.

2.text: Open the attack run; click again to drop the payload.

ca.title: Heavy Cruiser
ca.body: A large cruiser built around 203 mm-class guns: heavy alpha and AP that punches through most cruiser armour, usually with radar or hydroacoustics to win the information fight. Tougher than a light cruiser but still citadel-vulnerable up close, so she kites at range and trades in the gaps between enemy salvos.

cl.title: Light Cruiser
cl.body: A rapid-fire 152 mm gunboat: high damage per minute from volume of fire and HE, with smoke, hydroacoustics and good concealment as her tools. Thin armour and a shallow citadel make her easy to delete in a close-range duel, so she fights from cover and smoke; against heavy targets she leans on fires and torpedoes.

cruiser.title: Cruiser
cruiser.body: The middleweight: heavy cruisers (CA) trade rate of fire for shell weight, light cruisers (CL) trade punch for volume. Most carry radar or hydroacoustics, making them the team's scouts, destroyer hunters and anti-air escort; the shared weakness is thin armour — one battleship salvo can end them.

dd.title: Destroyer
dd.body: The stealth knife-fighter: a tiny silhouette, 5–7 km concealment, torpedoes for capital ships and smoke to disengage. Destroyers are the team's eyes — they spot, cap and contest — and the class most punished when overexposed: paper armour, no staying power, and radar strips away the concealment the whole playstyle rests on.

ss.title: Submarine
ss.body: The underwater assassin: the bow and stern torpedo tubes are her main battery, most of them acoustic homing — ping a target with sonar first and the torpedoes steer onto it; a second ping tightens the homing and makes the mark last longer.

1.text: Dive: at maximum depth only homing torpedoes remain and your own vision is nearly gone — fight on teammates' spotting.

2.text: Surface: at surface and periscope depth the deck gun and unguided torpedoes still work.

3.text: Clear the sonar mark you have put on a target.

ss.note: Diving drains the battery (it recharges on the surface). A hit while submerged damages the fuel system: surface or use Damage Control within about five seconds to stop the leak, or the spill betrays your position until you surface.

ballistics.sigmaHint: Tighter grouping — higher sigma means shells land closer to point of aim.
ballistics.horizontalDispHint: Maximum horizontal spread at the ship's gun range.
ballistics.delimRangeHint: Range at which the dispersion formula is anchored.
ballistics.massHint: Heavier shells retain velocity better at range.
ballistics.muzzleVelocityHint: Initial shell speed at the muzzle.
ballistics.airDragHint: How quickly the shell loses speed in flight. Lower = flatter trajectory.

consumables.keysHint: Keys follow the game's default consumable bindings (remappable in-game).

spec.hpHint: Total damage the ship can take before sinking.
spec.torpProtectionHint: Reduces torpedo damage to the citadel. Higher is better.
spec.citadelArmorHint: Maximum thickness of the citadel's armoured box. Protects against AP shells reaching the magazines/engine.
spec.bowArmorHint: Thickness of the extremities. Determines whether HE shells shatter and whether overmatch occurs.
spec.mainGunRangeHint: Maximum firing distance of the main battery.
spec.mainGunReloadHint: Time between full broadsides. Lower is better.
spec.mainGunCaliberHint: Shell diameter. Determines HE penetration (≈ caliber/6, or /4 for German HE) and AP overmatch.
spec.mainGunSigmaHint: Accuracy parameter — higher means tighter grouping.
spec.turretTraverseHint: Time to rotate turrets 180°. Lower is better.
spec.heShellHint: High-explosive per-shell damage. Causes fires and damages lightly-armoured targets.
spec.sapShellHint: Semi-armor-piercing — high damage vs light/medium armour, no fires.
spec.apShellHint: Armour-piercing per-shell damage. Highest damage against broadside armoured targets.
spec.shellSpeedHint: Initial shell speed. Higher = flatter trajectory, shorter lead time.
spec.hePenetrationHint: Armor HE can penetrate without shattering. Roughly caliber/6 (German: caliber/4).
spec.fireChanceHint: Per-shell probability of starting a fire.
spec.apRicochetAngleHint: Impact angle at which AP shells start to ricochet. Higher is better.
spec.apAlwaysRicochetAngleHint: Impact angle beyond which AP shells always ricochet. Higher is better.
spec.apNormalizationHint: Angle by which AP shells normalize against sloped armour. Higher is better.
spec.altFireHint: Alternate firing mode: quick burst salvoes with their own reload, range and shell performance.
spec.burstCountHint: Number of salvoes fired in one burst before the full reload. More is better.
spec.burstIntervalHint: Delay between the salvoes of one burst.
spec.deltaHint: Change versus the normal firing mode.
spec.torpDetectHint: Distance at which torpedoes become visible to the enemy. Lower gives less reaction time.
spec.torpFloodHint: Chance to start a flood on hit.
spec.torpFalloffHint: Damage coefficient by distance travelled: beyond each listed distance the listed ratio applies (most subs reach full damage from ~2.5 km; some ramp in tiers).
spec.torpDoublePingHint: Torpedo damage multiplier against a double-pinged target.
spec.torpHomingYawHint: How hard the torpedo turns toward a sonar mark (single/double mark, deg/s) — higher tracks harder turns.
spec.torpHomingCutoffHint: Inside this distance of the target the torpedo stops homing and runs straight (order: BB/CA/DD/Sub, double ping).
spec.rudderShiftHint: Time for the rudder to fully deflect. Lower = more agile.
spec.turningRadiusHint: Smaller radius = tighter turns. Affects dodging torpedoes and shells.
spec.surfaceDetectHint: Distance at which enemy surface ships spot you. Lower is better (stealthier).
spec.airDetectHint: Distance at which enemy aircraft spot you.
spec.sonarRangeHint: Maximum distance the sonar wave travels before dissipating.
spec.sonarWidthHint: Angular width of the sonar wave — wider is easier to hit with.
spec.sonarPing1Hint: How long the single-ping mark stays on the target after one sonar hit.
spec.sonarPing2Hint: How long the double-ping mark stays on the target after two consecutive sonar hits; longer than the single-ping mark.
spec.sonarMarkTimeHint: How long the sonar mark stays on the target (this client does not split single/double ping durations).
spec.batteryCapacityHint: The electricity reserve spent while submerged.
spec.shellDamageHint: Standard damage per hit of this shell type.
